note: THE ESCAPE THAT IS NOT A CHARACTER AT ALL. Emacs answers ("ab" 2): backslash-SPACE in a string reads as NOTHING -- it exists so a long string can be broken across source lines (backslash-newline does the same). It is measured here because it is the counterexample to "an unknown escape is the character itself": an implementation that made `\\ ' a space would silently change the text of every docstring that uses the continuation. kg refuses it as an unknown escape.
